## Conversation 10 — Fix the enemy collision test

### User prompt

> I got this,
>
> ```terminaloutput
> python module5/test_game.py 
> <frozen importlib._bootstrap>:488: RuntimeWarning: Your system is avx2 capable but pygame was not built with support for it. The performance of some of your blits could be adversely affected. Consider enabling compile time detection with environment variables like PYGAME_DETECT_AVX2=1 if you are compiling without cross compilation.
> pygame 2.6.1 (SDL 2.32.72, Python 3.13.15)
> Hello from the pygame community. https://www.pygame.org/contribute.html
> ..........F......
> ======================================================================
> FAIL: test_enemy_collision_causes_loss (__main__.GameTests.test_enemy_collision_causes_loss)
> Contact with the enemy transitions the game to its lost state.
> ----------------------------------------------------------------------
> Traceback (most recent call last):
>   File "/home/kyle/main/gitPrjs/Personal/gitOrgs/SNHU/cs-530-ai-principals-and-applications/module5/test_game.py", line 135, in test_enemy_collision_causes_loss
>     self.assertEqual(self.game.state, "lost")
>     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
> AssertionError: 'playing' != 'lost'
> - playing
> + lost
> ```

### Assistant response

> The failure is caused by the test changing the enemy's `rect` without changing its internal floating-point position. `Enemy.update()` resets the rectangle from that internal position before the collision check, undoing the test's placement.
>
> I fixed the test to create an enemy at the player's position through the `Enemy` constructor, so both representations start synchronized. This keeps the production game code unchanged.
